newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close slightly higher.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher on Sunday in anticipation that a meeting between Israel's prime minister, finance minister and central bank governor may yield a lower interest rate, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.09 pct to 105.18
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.08 to 104.07
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will meet Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel later on Sunday to discuss possible further cuts in the budget.
"There is some expectation (in the market) that because of the meeting interest rates may go down. People are turning to invest in bonds," said a trader at IBI Investment House.

The government will issue on Monday 400 million shekels worth of bonds instead of the usual 200 million shekels because markets will be closed next Monday due to the Jewish festival of Passover, traders said.
"Despite the big amount of bonds that will be put on the market, bonds did not perform weakly today," the IBI trader said.
She added that the price of dollar-linked bonds was going up because yields were at a high 6.6 percent.

"Some traders believe that maybe after today's meeting a cut in interest rates may be agreed upon which will improve the situation of the dollar," said Dan Shamir of Israel Discount Bank. "But in my mind the meeting will not assure a lower interest rate unless a further budget cut is made."
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
